hook.line: So I tried the ChatGPT trend...
hook.visual: Phone screen recording: a long 'show me what you look like' selfie prompt pasted into ChatGPT, sent within the first second, under a fixed title line.

beats.what: Prompt already typed in the ChatGPT box with the keyboard open; title 'So I tried the chatgbt trend...' sits mid-screen the whole video.
Prompt is sent and scrolls up as a blue chat bubble.
Image generation starts: the 'Sketching it out' status and a dotted placeholder.
Status changes to 'Making the first draft'; nothing to see yet, only the wait.
Status 'Setting the scene'; the scroll back to the prompt keeps the screen moving.
Status 'Adding final touches': the countdown is nearly over.
Reveal: a blurry, low-angle selfie of a real young man, apparently the creator himself, appears as ChatGPT's 'self-portrait'.

why_it_works: The app's own progress messages act as a countdown, so a 27 s wait becomes suspense with a guaranteed payoff.
Payoff withheld to the last 5 s, and the video ends right after it, so it loops into the wait again (loop 0.86).
The ambiguous reveal (is that ChatGPT or the creator?) plus the 'Who is that' caption drives comments (22.6k).
Rides a named trend, so viewers already know what result to wait for.
weaknesses: No voice and 27 s of near-static screen; it only works because the trend was already known.
Title text overlaps the prompt bubble and is cut off ('trend...'), and most text sits outside the safe area (0.929).
for_robert: Use a visible progress wait as suspense: show a tool 'thinking' while Fred fidgets or peeks at the screen, then cut out right after the reveal.
